name: Texas
feeText: Harris County District Clerk, fees due at filing of a new divorce suit, effective January 1, 2026: Divorce no children $350.00; Divorce with children $365.00 (includes the $15 domestic relations fee added to all cases involving children). Service fees not included. No separate fee for an answer is listed; a cross-action/counterclaim is $80.00.

waiver.name: Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs or an Appeal Bond (Tex. R. Civ. P. 145)

residency.text: Either spouse must have been a domiciliary of Texas for the preceding 6 months and a resident of the filing county for the preceding 90 days (Fam. Code § 6.301).

waitingPeriod.text: The court may not grant a divorce before the 60th day after the suit was filed, except in certain family-violence cases (Fam. Code § 6.702).

simplified.text: No summary or simplified divorce procedure in the Family Code; agreed divorces follow the ordinary procedure.

parentingClass.text: Not required statewide: in a suit affecting the parent-child relationship the court may order a parent education and family stabilization course of 4 to 12 hours (Fam. Code § 105.009); some counties require it by local rule.

uncertain: No statewide divorce filing fee: amount is the Harris County District Clerk's (most populous county); other counties differ.
statutes.capitol.texas.gov is a JavaScript app; text of Fam. Code ch. 6 and ch. 105 read from the legislature's static copy at tcss.legis.texas.gov/resources/FA/htm/.
txcourts.gov blocked the automated download of the waiver form; the form name and URL come from the official site's index, not from the PDF text.
Response fee: no answer fee appears in the Harris County schedule; set to null.
Local-rule parenting class requirements in individual counties not verified.
